required_fixes: Broaden the basis-of-preparation/materiality narrative to cover all material sustainability-related risks and opportunities (not only climate), or explicitly scope and justify if only climate is material (without introducing any 'data unavailable' language).
Add an explicit identification of the related financial statements (eg, consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024) to satisfy IFRS S1.22.

Add a clear statement identifying the standards/guidance applied in preparing the sustainability-related financial disclosures (eg, IFRS S1 and IFRS S2; and any other frameworks used such as NGFS/IEA/PCAF), and identify any SASB topics/metrics considered (or state they were considered and deemed not applicable), to address IFRS S1.55, S1.58 and S1.59.

Add an explicit statement that for climate-related risks/opportunities the entity applied the specifically applicable IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard (IFRS S2) to determine disclosure requirements (IFRS S1.56).

If cross-references are used elsewhere in the report, describe them and confirm they meet IFRS S1 cross-reference requirements; if none are used, state that no information is incorporated by cross-reference (IFRS S1.63).
Address subsequent events and authorisation-for-issue considerations (IFRS S1.67–68) with a policy statement (and, if applicable, disclosures), avoiding any invented 'missing data' statements.
Clarify applicability for reporting-period-change and interim-reporting requirements (IFRS S1.66 and S1.69) by stating whether such circumstances occurred/elected in the period.
Add verifiable evidence or cross-references for the claim that sustainability disclosures are reported at the same time as the financial statements (dates/approval/filing).
For scenario resilience statements, add quantified results and the Pillar 2 threshold values (or clearly state that the assessment is qualitative and provide the basis/criteria).
Define 'material' for disorderly scenario impacts and provide scenario output ranges supporting the conclusion and the post-2030 buffer statement.
Reconcile or explain the two board climate expertise percentages (33.5% vs 37.5%) with clear definitions and scope.
Complete the 5×5 risk-matrix banding so every possible score is classified (explicitly address 7 and 13–14).
Add definitions/methodologies for green loans %, carbon intensity, and the anti-double-counting control for market-based Scope 2.

Remove or generalize hard-coded reporting years, specific dates, currencies, and detailed numeric values from the basis-of-preparation narrative. Replace with configurable placeholders or generic descriptions (e.g., 'the reporting period', 'the presentation currency') so the section can function as a reusable general requirements template.

Refocus the section on basis-of-preparation principles and mechanics. Move detailed topic content (e.g., specific climate risks, scenario outcomes, emissions values, green loan percentages, Tier 1 capital amounts) to the relevant Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, and Metrics and Targets sections, and replace them here with brief, generic examples plus cross-references (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Risk Management]').

Introduce a short bulleted list of qualitative preparation principles and key characteristics near the start of the section (e.g., consistency with financial statements, neutrality, completeness, use of estimates, comparability) to align with the layered structure requirement.

Add explicit connectivity sentences at the end of each major subsection using the standard cross-reference placeholder format (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Governance] for detailed oversight disclosures' or 'See [Section: Metrics and Targets] for full emissions metrics and targets.').

Where scenario analysis, risk ratings, and other forward-looking or model-based content are retained, explicitly label them as estimates or forward-looking assessments and use cautious modality ('could', 'may', 'is expected to') while distinguishing them from current-period facts.
Shorten and split long sentences, particularly in subsections 1.3 and 1.4, to maintain clear subject–verb–object structure and align with the short-to-medium sentence length guidance.

Separate 'principles/what' from 'mechanics/how' within subsections using brief subheadings or clearly delineated paragraphs (e.g., 'Principles for risk rating' vs 'Methodology applied to the climate risk register').

Introduce at least one compact, captioned table where numeric groupings are presented (e.g., emissions data-quality characteristics or scope emissions breakdown), and number and reference it in the narrative in line with the table/figure captioning rules.

Clarify treatment of missing or incomplete data, if applicable, by explicitly stating when information is not available or under development, including reason, interim approach, limitations, and planned enhancements, to comply with the missing data protocol even if the current period has no major gaps.

Replace explanatory meta-language such as 'This subsection explains...' with more direct disclosure language (e.g., 'We disclose...', 'We describe...') to better match the standards-aligned, audit-ready voice.

section_generation_score.policy: Missing requirements reduce audit/readiness visibility only; they must not appear in report prose.
